lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Lourdes, this is Daniela. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the overnight fast went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about fruit at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Pretty good actually.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's great to hear.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to finish eating by 8 on 4 nights?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 2.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This feels really necessary to you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're giving everything to work right now, and there's not much left over for you.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I told my family I'm done eating at 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You said the same thing last week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That sounds like an excuse to me.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody keeps telling me that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to finish eating by 8 on 5 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 2 out of 4 days, the hard part was the hunger at night, and next week you're going to finish eating by 8 on 5 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Lourdes, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Asks about fruit at night; not addressed later

flags.reason: Participant raised a fruit-at-night question at line 4; coach asked a generic check-in and never returned to it.
Right after change talk at line 27, coach pushed a follow-through label instead of reinforcing or exploring.
Fear-based health warning given without permission; participant responded with ambivalence.
Labeled participant's hesitation as an excuse, which likely increases resistance.
Directive 'You have to' statement; repeated persuading pattern in lines 28-36 with sustain talk rising.

score.summary: Coach used good reflections and a clear goal-setting structure, and Lourdes ended with a concrete 5-night goal and a barrier plan. However, a run of persuading and labeling (lines 28-36) pushed back against her ambivalence and her fruit question was never addressed.
strengths: Line 13-14: complex reflection captured Lourdes's health motivation well.
Line 24: asked permission before sharing a suggestion.
Line 42: clear summary that let Lourdes confirm the goal and barrier plan.
coaching_tips: Line 28-36: after change talk ('I'll set an alarm,' 'this week I'll really do it'), reflect rather than persuade; try 'What would help you make that stick?'
Line 34: avoid labeling hesitation as an excuse; reflect the ambivalence instead, e.g., 'Part of you is unsure this will work.'
Line 5: return to Lourdes's fruit question at line 4 before moving on, or ask permission to address it now.
